wiki_text: Shannon LNG (the Shannon Technology and Energy Park at Tarbert/Ballylongford on the Shannon Estuary, Co. Kerry) is developed by Shannon LNG Ltd, a subsidiary of US-based New Fortress Energy (NFE). The project has been pursued since 2005. An Bord Pleanala (ABP) refused planning permission for the ~EUR 650 million development in October 2023, finding it 'contrary to Government policy.' In September 2024 the High Court (Humphreys J.) quashed that refusal, holding the policy basis was an interpretation rather than a formal State directive, and remitted the matter. In March 2025 ABP withdrew its application for leave to appeal the High Court judgment, leaving the quashing in place. Also in March 2025, ABP/An Coimisiun Pleanala granted permission for a 600 MW gas-fired power plant and 120 MW battery energy storage system at the site (with a 10-year construction window and operation limited to backup-to-renewables until end-2050); that power-plant permission is itself subject to judicial review by Friends of the Irish Environment. On 30 May 2025 Shannon LNG reactivated its application for the broader development (FSRU, jetty, onshore receiving facilities, power plant, BESS); a decision was expected later in 2025, with updated information to be resubmitted. As of this sweep the LNG import terminal itself remains without final planning approval.

topic: State-led Strategic Gas Emergency Reserve (SGER) - approval, site, scope
wiki_text: This GEM record corresponds to Ireland's State-led Strategic Gas Emergency Reserve (SGER). The Irish Government approved the SGER on 5 March 2025, deciding it should take the form of a Floating Storage and Regasification Unit (FSRU) owned and operated by Gas Networks Ireland (GNI) on behalf of the State. It is explicitly framed as a non-commercial, emergency-only, transitional measure (to reduce stranded-asset risk and not to support increased gas demand) - a posture consistent with Ireland's standing opposition (since 2020) to commercial/'fracked-gas' LNG imports. On 26 November 2025, after assessing 14 candidate coastal locations, GNI announced the selected site: Cahiracon, Co. Clare, on the Shannon Estuary. The site is to host a deep-water jetty for the FSRU, an onshore facility, and a new connection to the national gas transmission network. The FSRU is described as ~300 m in length holding up to ~170,000 m3 of LNG (roughly six months' supply for ~200,000 average households). This State project is distinct from the commercial proposals (NFE's Shannon LNG, Predator's Mag Mell, Pilot LNG's Cork FSRU).

topic: Mag Mell FSRU dormant; sponsor pivot to Morocco/Trinidad
wiki_text: Predator Oil & Gas Holdings Plc's 'Mag Mell' FSRU concept proposed mooring FSRU(s) ~50 km off the Co. Cork coast and bringing gas ashore via the disused Kinsale Head pipeline. The proposal has shown no substantive progress in Ireland for over two years and is presumed shelved. Predator's operational focus has shifted to Morocco and Trinidad; the company indicated it may repurpose the Mag Mell FSRU technical/regulatory/commercial template for a Moroccan natural-gas infrastructure tender, targeting registration of an Expression of Interest by 23 July 2025. Ireland's continued policy resistance to commercial LNG imports (and the State's own emergency-only SGER) further reduces the near-term prospects for a commercial Mag Mell development.
